newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says supports Thai authorities on baht.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says supports Thai authorities on baht.

text.p: Malaysian Acting Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday that his government was willing to support the Thai authorities on the baht.
"We will give whatever assistance or support that is necessary," Anwar told reporters when asked whether he was concerned over any spill-over effect of the Thai's float of the baht on Wednesday.
"We have full confidence in the Thai economy, they are managing well," he said after officiating a conference on urban life.
Asked about whether the Malaysian central bank, Bank Negara would intervene again to protect the ringgit, Anwar said: "I trust in the wisdom of Bank Negara".
Bank Negara on Wednesday intervened in the market by buying ringgit and selling dollars, using its own name to defend the currency against an attack soon after news of the Thai baht's float.
Asked about Malaysian interest-rate direction, Anwar said: "I have full confidence in Bank Negara to manage monetary policy and they keep me informed from time to time."
Malaysian interbank interest rates have been trending lower in the last few weeks after surging in May following the Thai baht crisis. They are now near pre-Thai crisis levels.

But economists have said that Malaysia cannot afford to lower its interest rates too much just yet, as the government wants to keep costs high for currency speculators who may want to hold short-ringgit positions.
A high interest rate regime would also help to bring the booming Malaysian economy to a soft landing.
